text: Eclectic means made up of many different kinds of things. Astronomers expected a mixed group of stars, galaxies, and clouds, but not these dots.
To envelop something is to wrap all the way around it. Here, a thick cloud of gas envelops the black hole like a cocoon.
To contend is to argue that something is true. Here, a scientist contends that another team's way of measuring does not work.
The JWST is a huge space camera that orbits the Sun, far from Earth. It sees faint, very old light from the early universe.
A telescope is a tool that makes faraway things look closer and clearer.
An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars, planets, and space.
To orbit is to travel around something in a curved path, the way Earth goes around the Sun.
A high-resolution camera takes very sharp pictures with lots of tiny details.
Nebulae are giant clouds of gas and dust in space. Some of them are where new stars are born.
A galaxy is a huge group of billions of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
The Milky Way is our home galaxy. Earth and the Sun are inside it.
Tinted means having a light touch of color. A red tinge is a slight reddish look.
Jargon is special words that people in one job or hobby use, which outsiders may not know.
Technical means about the special details of a science, machine, or skill.
A black hole is a place in space where so much mass is squeezed together that its gravity pulls in everything nearby, even light.
Supermassive means super heavy. Supermassive black holes weigh as much as millions or billions of Suns.
Unprecedented means never happening before. These black holes are growing faster than anything seen before.
Violent means extremely forceful and wild. Here it describes very fast, powerful growth.
A growth spurt is a short time of very fast growing, like when a kid suddenly shoots up a few inches.
Bizarre means very strange and hard to explain.
Fierce means very strong and intense. A fierce debate is one where people argue hard.
A debate is a discussion where people with different ideas argue their sides.
The origins of something are where and how it began.
To emit is to send out, like a lamp emitting light.
A wavelength is the distance from the top of one wave to the top of the next. For light, it decides the color.
The cosmic dawn is the early time when the first stars and galaxies were lighting up the young universe.
The letters bn mean billion, and 500m means 500 million. So 13.4bn years is 13.4 billion years.
The Big Bang is the huge explosion of space and energy that scientists think started the universe about 13.8 billion years ago.
This is a playful way to say the dots seem to look at you from every picture.
To coin a word is to invent it or use it for the first time.
Populous means having lots of members. A populous galaxy has a huge number of stars.
Mature means fully grown and developed.
To dub something is to give it a nickname.
This nickname means the dots seemed to break scientists' ideas about how old the universe is.
To imply is to suggest something without saying it directly.
A spectrum is light spread out into its separate colors, like in a rainbow. Scientists can read patterns in it.
Hydrogen is the lightest and most common element in the universe. Stars are mostly made of it.
Gravity is the pull that objects with mass have on each other. It keeps you on the ground.
To disfavour an idea is to make it look less likely to be true.
Concentrated means packed closely into a small space.
Paradoxical means seeming to contradict itself, like a black hole that glows.
Accretion is when a black hole pulls in matter, like gas, and it piles up around the hole. It heats up and glows.
Radiation is energy that travels through space, such as light and X-rays.
Intense means very strong.
An active galactic nucleus, or AGN, is the glowing center of a galaxy where a supermassive black hole is feeding on gas.
Here the doughnut is a ring of gas and dust circling a black hole, shaped like a doughnut.
In space, dust is tiny bits of solid stuff, made of heavier elements.
Heavy elements are materials such as carbon and iron. They are made inside stars, so the very early universe had few.
A cocoon is a wrapping, like the one a caterpillar makes. Here it is a thick gas cloud around the black hole.
Reddened means turned redder. Light passing through gas can lose its blue and look redder.
X-rays are a kind of light with very short wavelengths that our eyes cannot see.
An advocate is someone who speaks up for an idea.
Infalling means falling inward, toward the center.
To scramble is to move fast and a bit clumsily in a hurry.
Occam's razor is a rule of thumb that says the simpler explanation, with fewer guesses, is the one to try first.
The appeal of something is what makes people like it.
Imaginative means full of creative new ideas.
To concede is to admit that something is true, even if you did not want to.
Nomenclature is the system of names used in a subject, like names for new objects.
A novelty is something new and unusual.
Nuclear fusion is when tiny atoms smash together and make lots of energy. It is what powers the Sun.
A proponent is a person who supports an idea.
Distinctive means easy to recognize because it is different from others.
Satisfactorily means in a way that is good enough. Neither idea explains everything satisfactorily.
A critic is someone who points out what is wrong with an idea.
An assumption is something you accept as true without proof.
To forbid is to not allow. Here, the model says a thing can't happen.
To settle a matter is to end the argument by finding the answer.
One order of magnitude means about ten times bigger. Several orders means thousands of times or more.
A solar mass is the weight of our Sun. So 50m solar masses means 50 million Suns.
To infer is to figure something out from clues instead of seeing it directly.
Controversial means that people disagree about it.
A data point is one measurement. One alone cannot prove much.
Vindication means being proved right. Scientists want that for their idea.
If something is at stake, it could be won or lost depending on the outcome.
To put on weight is to gain mass. Here it asks how the first black holes got so heavy.
To punch above your weight is to matter more than your small size suggests, like a small boxer who beats bigger ones.

t: People see what they want to see
forms: People see what they want to see
text: This means people often read the same facts in a way that supports what they already believe.
